# Independent package-signature vector

`openssl-envelope.json` signs the exact bytes in `openssl-claims.json`, using an
ephemeral Ed25519 key generated by OpenSSL 3.2.4 (11 February 2025). The raw
32-byte public key is retained as standard padded base64 in
`openssl-public-key.txt`. No private key is retained.

The generator constructed DSSE PAE independently of `latent-signing`:

```text
DSSEv1 SP decimal(type UTF-8 byte length) SP type SP decimal(payload byte length) SP payload
```

OpenSSL `pkeyutl -sign -rawin` signed these bytes, and
`pkeyutl -verify -pubin -keyform DER -rawin` verified them before retention.
The envelope's key hint is SHA-256 of the raw public key. Claims reference the
exact maintained `examples/package-format/browser-assets/manifest.json` bytes.
The times 1000 and 2000 are synthetic test times, not current authorization.

Tests verify this external vector through the public package verifier and
separately validate the wire schemas. This supplements RFC 8032 Ed25519 vectors;
it does not claim generic DSSE conformance or trust the fixture's publisher.
